payload.author: plengauer
payload.body:
@copilot here's what this PR needs before it's mergeable:

**1. Fix the `hello world 7` / `hello world 6` mismatch in `tests/auto/test_auto_injection_docker.sh`.** This single change is the root cause of both failing smoke jobs *and* the one open review thread, so fixing it closes all of them at once.

The Dockerfile written at line 56 still emits `hello world 6`:

```sh
echo 'ENTRYPOINT ["node", "-e", "console.log(\"hello world 6\")"]' >>"$dockerfile"
```

but line 59 was changed to expect `hello world 7`:

```sh
assert_equals "hello world 7" "$(sudo docker run --rm=true docker_test_0)"
```

The container prints `hello world 6`, the assertion wants `hello world 7`, so the script exits 1. CI confirms it is the comparison and not the `docker run`: the last span emitted before the failure is `sudo docker run --rm=true docker_test_0` at `auto/test_auto_injection_docker.sh:59` with `shell.command.exit_code: 0`, and the root script span is the only one with `status_code: ERROR`.

Preferred fix: bump the ENTRYPOINT at line 56 to print `hello world 7`, rather than reverting the assertion back to `6`. Renumbering is what the rest of the PR implies, because the new combined-flag test you added around line 38 already claims the `hello world 6` label:

```sh
assert_equals "hello world 6" "$(sudo docker run -Pi --no-healthcheck --oom-kill-disable --read-only --sig-proxy debian:latest echo hello world 6)"
```

Reverting the assertion instead would leave two different tests both asserting on `hello world 6`, which is exactly the collision the renumbering was meant to avoid.

This also resolves the open thread at https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/pull/4146#discussion_r3846019894 — please reply there once it's fixed.

Failing jobs on `a80ef2c`:
- `ci / shell / smoke (ubuntu-latest)` — https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32756238052/job/97636262881
- `ci / shell / smoke (ubuntu-24.04-arm)` — https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32756238052/job/97636262868
- `ci / all` — https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32756238052/job/97781698238 — this is the aggregate gate; it fails only because of the two smoke jobs above and should go green on its own once they do. No separate fix needed.

**2. Nothing to change for the `copilot-pull-request-reviewer` check** — https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32756987586/job/97526713437. It failed because the agentic review didn't get a runner before its timeout, not because of anything in this diff. Please don't chase it from this PR; it's a repository CI-configuration matter (a `copilot-code-review.yml` specifying `runs-on`), and it is being left as-is here rather than reran.

For context on the rest of the PR: the branch is **not** conflicted with `main` (`mergeable_state` is `blocked`, purely on the failing checks above), and every other check on the head commit is green or skipped — including the new `-Pi --no-healthcheck --oom-kill-disable --read-only --sig-proxy` injection test, which passed. Item 1 is the only code change needed.

payload.body:
@copilot here's what this PR needs before it's mergeable. All three items live in the same three lines of `meta/debian/postinst` you changed, so they're best done together.

1. **The deb smoke test genuinely fails — the new install path leaves the versioned Python tree unusable.** `ci / shell / smoke` fails on both [`ubuntu-latest`](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32750968734/job/97636572504) and [`ubuntu-24.04-arm`](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32750968734/job/97636572493) with `Process completed with exit code 1`, and it is not flaky — same failure, same place, on both architectures. The failing assertion is in `tests/auto/test_auto_injection_python.sh`, the first block after `export OTEL_SHELL_CONFIG_INJECT_DEEP=TRUE`:

   ```sh
   echo 'import requests
   requests.get("http://example.com/foo")' | python3 | grep -- '/foo' || exit 1
   ```

   `grep` exits 1 — no HTTP span was emitted at all. Note the test's own guard at the top means `/usr/share/opentelemetry_shell/agent.instrumentation.python/<X.Y>/` *does* exist (otherwise the test would have skipped), so the directory survived but its `site-packages` tree is no longer importable for deep injection after the new postinst runs.

   The most likely cause is that `pip install --upgrade --no-compile --target "$target"` now writes straight into the live shipped tree. pip does not treat packages already present in a `--target` directory as installed, so it re-resolves the whole requirements set from the network, and `--upgrade` deletes the existing per-package directories before writing. The old code deliberately avoided both problems: it pre-seeded a throwaway venv from the archived tarball (so pip had nothing left to resolve and worked offline) and merged back with a *non-destructive* `cp -r -u`. With the venv gone, a partial or failed install now corrupts the shipped tree in place, and the `_python_keep_archived=true` fallback just `continue`s — it no longer protects anything, because the damage has already been done. Please inspect what `<X.Y>/site-packages` actually contains after postinst on a runner, and make the install either offline-satisfiable against the archived tree or non-destructive to it.

2. **Split the chained condition — a `compileall` failure currently deletes a working install.** See [this thread](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/pull/4140#discussion_r3845719178) on `meta/debian/postinst:79`. `! type python$version || ! pip install ... || ! compileall ...` collapses three unrelated failures into one branch, so a `compileall` failure triggers the same `rm -rf` of the entire version directory as a missing interpreter — even though the package install succeeded. Beyond diagnosability in dpkg logs, that is a real behavior change: bytecode precompilation is an optimization and should not be able to remove instrumentation. Split it into sequential, individually named steps with a step-specific message, and let the failure handling differ per step.

3. **Guard pip availability instead of assuming it.** See [this thread](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/pull/4140#discussion_r3845719099) on the same line. The success condition moved from "`pythonX.Y -m venv` works" to "`pythonX.Y -m pip` is importable". On Debian/Ubuntu an interpreter is commonly present without pip, and the `venv` path you removed could bootstrap it via `ensurepip`. Either probe `python$version -m pip --version` and fall back to `python$version -m ensurepip`, or treat "pip missing" exactly like the old "venv missing" case, so instrumentation isn't deleted for an interpreter that exists. This may well be the same root cause as item 1, so it's worth checking first.

Doing item 2 first will also make item 1's failure mode legible the next time it happens, rather than surfacing as a bare exit code 1.

payload.body:
@copilot here's what this PR needs before it's mergeable:

1. **Fix the `ci / build / build-workflow-image` failure — this is the merge blocker.** ([failing job](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32753376718/job/97634097112)) The new site-packages extraction in `meta/debian/postinst` breaks under Alpine's busybox `tar`, so `apk add` fails:

   ```
   * tar: ./3.14/site-packages: not found in archive
   ERROR: lib/apk/exec/opentelemetry-shell-5.61.0-r0.post-install: exited with error 1
   ```

   Root cause: `merge-python-site-packages` in `.github/workflows/build.yml` builds the archive with `find . -type f -print0 | xargs -0 sha256sum | ... | tar -cf python_site_packages.tar -T -`, so `python_site_packages.tar.xz` contains **only regular-file members** — there is no `./3.14/site-packages` directory entry in it. GNU tar treats that argument as a path prefix and extracts everything beneath it, but busybox `tar` on Alpine requires the named member to actually exist, so it errors and the post-install exits 1. (`build-apk` appends `meta/debian/postinst` verbatim as the apk `post-install`, which is why only the Alpine path trips on this — the deb `verify-*` jobs never install.) Note the version-detection line just above does *not* protect you here: it derives available versions from file paths via `cut -d / -f 2`, so it correctly reports `3.14` as present and the `-ge 0` guard passes. Fix by selecting members with a pattern that matches files rather than a directory — e.g. `'./3.'"$python3_archived_minor"'/site-packages/*'` — or by emitting directory entries when the tar is created; either way please verify it under busybox tar, not just GNU tar. `ci / all` is failing only as a downstream consequence of this job, so it should clear itself.

2. **Add `--no-deps` to the lock install in `build-python-site-packages`** ([thread](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/pull/4139#discussion_r3846047439)) — `.github/workflows/build.yml` runs `pip3 install -r requirements.lock.txt` without `--no-deps`, so pip still performs dependency resolution and can pull in anything the lock happens to miss. That undercuts the determinism this PR exists for, and it's inconsistent with `postinst`, which does pass `--no-deps`. Add `--no-deps` and follow it with `pip3 check` so an incomplete lock fails the build loudly instead of silently drifting.

3. **Force wheels when building the wheelhouse** ([thread](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/pull/4139#discussion_r3846047487)) — the `build-deb` step runs `pip3 download -r requirements.lock.txt -d .../wheels` with no `--only-binary`, so sdists can land in the wheelhouse. The offline path then runs `pip install --no-deps --no-index --find-links .../wheels`, which would have to build those sdists on the target machine with no guaranteed toolchain — precisely the "offline-first from shipped wheels" guarantee this PR is making. Add `--only-binary=:all:` (so a missing wheel fails the build rather than shipping a broken wheelhouse) and `--no-deps`. While you're in this step: the wheels are downloaded using the runner's single default interpreter and platform, but they're installed against whatever Python the target has (3.10–3.14, glibc or musl), so any non-pure-Python wheel here — `grpcio`, `protobuf`, `wrapt` — will not match at install time and will silently fall through to the network fallback. Please make the download cover the interpreters/platforms you actually ship for, or restrict the wheelhouse to the pure-Python subset so the fallback is the intended path rather than an accident.

Items 2 and 3 touch the same two `build.yml` steps and are worth folding into a single change; item 1 is independent and is what's actually keeping the PR red.

This environment has no PR-edit MCP tool, no GitHub token, and `gh` is not authenticated, so I can’t directly mutate the PR description from here without a supported update tool.

The corrected PR body should be:

```md
`cache_restore_fast()` extracted tar archives without `-C /`, so relative member paths (e.g. `../../../../../var/cache/apt/archives/...`) resolved against the action's CWD instead of the filesystem root. The restore appeared to succeed (exit 0), blocking the `@actions/cache` fallback, while files landed in a garbage path under `_actions/`. Every run effectively did a full cold install.

## Changes

- **Root cause — wrong extraction directory**: Added `-C /` to both `tar` invocations in `cache_restore_fast`:

  ```sh
  # before
  sudo tar -P --use-compress-program="zstd -d --long=30" -xf "$tmpfile"
  # after
  sudo tar -C / -P --use-compress-program="zstd -d --long=30" -xf "$tmpfile"
  ```

  `/` is the correct target because the `@actions/cache` entries carry `../../../../../var/cache/apt/archives/...`-style member paths, and `..` at the filesystem root resolves back to `/`, so `/var/cache/apt/archives/...` is hit regardless of how deep the workspace sits.

- **Spurious `Permission denied` + over-broad match on `find`**: Changed the write-back check from unprivileged `find /var/cache/apt/archives/ -name '*.deb'` (fails on `partial/`, matches unrelated debs) to `sudo find /var/cache/apt/archives/ -maxdepth 1 -name 'opentelemetry-shell_*.deb' 2>/dev/null`.

- **Unquoted glob expanding to multiple args**: Replaced all bare `opentelemetry-shell_*_*.deb` globs passed to `[ -r ]`, `dpkg-deb`, and `apt-get` with a single resolved variable:

  ```sh
  deb_file="$(sudo find /var/cache/apt/archives/ -maxdepth 1 -name 'opentelemetry-shell_*.deb' 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -n 1)"
  if ! type otel.sh && [ -n "$deb_file" ] && [ -r "$deb_file" ]; then
  ```

  Two or more cached versions no longer cause a silent `[: too many arguments` failure that falls through to cold install.

- Fixes #4044
```

payload.author: plengauer
payload.body:
@copilot this PR has review feedback that needs addressing:

- [#discussion_r3845802992](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/pull/4134#discussion_r3845802992) (and the identical change at [#discussion_r3845803026](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/pull/4134#discussion_r3845803026)) — in `meta/debian/postinst`, going from `xargs -r -P 0 tar ...` to `xargs -r -n 1 -P 0 tar ...` turns one batched extraction into one `tar` per version, and each of those re-decompresses the whole archive from the start rather than sharing a single pass. With `zstd -d --long=27` every worker also allocates a ~128 MiB decompression window, and the node and python blocks run concurrently, so an unbounded `-P 0` can put real memory/IO pressure on `dpkg configure` on a small machine. Please cap the fanout (e.g. `-P "$(nproc)"` or a small fixed number) and re-examine whether `-n 1` is actually a win: N full decompression passes may cost more total CPU than the single pass it replaced, which cuts against this PR's stated perf goal. Whichever way you go, say why in the PR description.

- [#discussion_r3845803064](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/pull/4134#discussion_r3845803064) — in `.github/workflows/build.yml`, `xz -9 node_modules.tar` deleted its input, but `zstd -19 --long=27 -T0 node_modules.tar` does not, so the job now keeps both the uncompressed tar and the `.zst` on disk. The uploaded artifact itself is fine (the `path:` is explicit), but this is wasted workspace disk on the largest archives in the build. Add `--rm` to the `zstd` invocation (or `rm` the tar right after) in both the `merge-node-modules` and `merge-python-site-packages` steps.

The two regex comments on `postinst` (`.(xz|zst)$` vs `\.(xz|zst)$`) have been resolved as non-issues — the unescaped dot matches the convention already used by the adjacent filters on those same lines, and nothing in those directories can match it by accident. No action needed there.

@copilot here's what this PR needs before it's mergeable. Every red check and 22 of the 23 open review threads trace back to one mistake, so please fix it once, properly:

**1. The bracket-spacing normalization was applied to shell `test` expressions, not just YAML sequences.** `[` is a POSIX shell *command*: it needs a space after `[` and before `]`. `[-r foo]` and `["$a" -ge "$b"]` are not valid shell. Only real YAML flow sequences/mappings (`matrix:`, `needs:`, `[ 'amd64', ... ]`) should have been reformatted. Please restore the original spacing (or switch to `test ...`) at:

- `.github/workflows/build.yml` — line 68 (`[-r src/usr/share/opentelemetry_shell/agent.instrumentation.http/libinjecthttpheader.so]`), 190, 194, 328, 438, 472, 563, plus the `echo`-generated RPM scriptlets around 613, 618, 622, 627, 635 (`echo "if [\"\$1\" = 0] ..."`) — those emit broken shell *into* the generated `.spec`, so they fail at package install time rather than in CI.
- Line 472 specifically (`["${#command}" -gt 1] && printf ... || true`) is worth calling out: it doesn't fail the job because of the trailing `|| true`, it just silently makes `verify-deb-dependencies` stop checking anything.
- `.github/workflows/test_github.yml` — lines 116, 450, 470, 638, 651, 666, 845, 887, 906, 940, including the two commented-out `# ["$job_span_count" -ge 1]` / `# ["$empty_parent_count" -eq 1]` lines so they're still valid when re-enabled.
- Leave `jq '.workflow_runs[] | [.id, .run_attempt]'` (test_github.yml ~838 / ~880) as-is — that one really is a jq array literal, not a shell test.

**2. Failing checks that should clear once the above is fixed** (all on head `c5af580`):

- `ci / build / build-http` — all six matrix arches (amd64, arm64/v8, mips64le, ppc64le, riscv64, s390x) exit 127 with `line 4: [-r: command not found` — https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32750816586/job/97507096969

payload.author: plengauer
payload.body:
@copilot this PR has a failing check that needs fixing:

- **`ci / shell / install-manual-user`** — fails in the step `cat INSTALL.sh | sh -e` with exit code 123. See [job 97783472733](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32750078063/job/97783472733). This is what blocks the merge: `shell` fails → `join` is skipped → the `ci / all` gate fails because `needs.join.outputs.success` is empty.

  The failure chain inside `INSTALL.sh`:

  1. `curl -L ... https://api.github.com/repos/plengauer/opentelemetry-shell/releases/latest | jq '.assets[] | ...'` got a response with no `.assets` array (an API error/rate-limit body, not a release object), so jq emitted `jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Cannot iterate over null (null)`.
  2. The trailing `jq .browser_download_url -r` then printed the literal string `null`. `xargs -r` only skips *empty* input, not the text `null`, so it still ran `wget -O "$package" null` → `wget: unable to resolve host address 'null'`.
  3. `xargs` exited 123 and, because the script runs under `set -e` / `sh -e`, it aborted right there — so the three `if ! [ -r "$package" ]` fallback paths further down (direct release download, arch-independent package, old release format) never got a chance to run, even though they exist precisely for this case.

  Note the trigger is **not** this PR's diff (which only touches `.github/workflows/refresh_demos.yml`), and it may well have been a transient unauthenticated GitHub API rate limit — so it is possible a fresh run of this job passes on its own. But step 2 and 3 above are a genuine robustness bug regardless: an unavailable API makes `INSTALL.sh` die instead of falling back. Worth fixing in `INSTALL.sh` so the fallbacks actually engage:

  - emit nothing instead of `null` for a missing URL, e.g. `jq -r '.browser_download_url // empty'`, so `xargs -r` correctly skips it;
  - don't let the API pipeline's non-zero exit abort the script under `set -e` (guard it with an `if`, or append `|| true`), so control reaches the existing `if ! [ -r "$package" ]` fallbacks.

No merge conflict on this PR, and no unresolved review threads — the failing check above is the only thing outstanding.

payload.author: plengauer
payload.body:
@copilot Two things before this is mergeable:

1. **Please revert the `INSTALL.sh` changes.** This PR is scoped to YAML schema compliance per the description ("updates the affected YAML files... without changing intended behavior"), but `INSTALL.sh` isn't YAML and the description explicitly claims no behavior change — yet this file changes the release-fetch repo (`opentelemetry-shell` → `Thoth`), adds extension validation, and reworks the curl/jq/wget error handling. That's out of scope for this PR and undocumented in the description. Please drop it here and, if it's worth doing, open it as its own PR with its own rationale.

2. **On the `on:` quoting** — is there a way to disable v8r's schema check specifically for workflow files instead of quoting `on:` in every workflow file? `on:` only needs quoting here because v8r resolves the bare key to a YAML 1.1 boolean before validating against the generic github-workflow schema — that's a v8r/MegaLinter artifact, not something GitHub's own Actions runner cares about (it special-cases `on:` regardless of quoting). Please research whether something like this in `.mega-linter.yml` works:
   ```yaml
   YAML_V8R_FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE: "\\.github/workflows/"
   ```
   (mirrors the pattern already used for `SPELL_LYCHEE_FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE` in this same file). That would skip v8r's generic schema validation for workflow files specifically while actionlint/zizmor keep validating them properly, and `on:` could stay unquoted — matching every example in this repo's own README. If that works, use it instead of the per-file quoting on the workflow files. If it doesn't, explain why not.

@copilot this PR has failing checks that need fixing:

- **`ci / shell / install-manual-os (alpine:3.24)`** — [job log](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32749788035/job/97650859673). The failure is in `INSTALL.sh`, in the primary "install from the releases API" pipeline (`curl -L ... /releases/latest | jq '.assets[] | select(...)' | ... | jq .browser_download_url -r | xargs -r wget -O "$package"`). The API response came back without an `assets` array, so jq reported `Cannot iterate over null (null)`; the final `jq .browser_download_url -r` then printed the literal string `null`, and `xargs -r wget` tried to fetch `http://null/` → `wget: unable to resolve host address 'null'` → exit 123. Because of `set -e` at the top of the script, that non-zero exit kills the script immediately, so none of the three `if ! [ -r "$package" ]; then ... falling back ...` blocks below it ever run — the fallbacks that exist precisely for "failed to use API" are unreachable. Please make that first pipeline null-safe and non-fatal: `xargs -r` only guards against *empty* input, and `jq -r` on `null` emits the 4-character string `null`, not empty. Guard on `.assets` actually being present, drop a `null`/empty `browser_download_url` before it reaches `wget`, and let a failure there fall through to the existing fallbacks instead of aborting the script. Separately, worth making consistent while you're in there: the primary API call still targets the old repo name `plengauer/opentelemetry-shell`, while all three fallbacks already use `plengauer/Thoth`.

- **`ci / all`** — [job log](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32749788035/job/97782053473). No separate fix needed. It fails by design — `[ "$SUCCESS" = 'true' ]` with an empty `SUCCESS`, because `ci / join` was skipped once `ci / shell` failed. It should go green on its own once the job above passes.

For context so this doesn't get chased in the wrong place: neither failure comes from this PR's diff. `INSTALL.sh` isn't touched here, and the other ten `install-manual-os` matrix legs — including `alpine:3.21` and `alpine:3.23` — passed with the same script within minutes, so the trigger looks like a transient or rate-limited API response rather than a code change. The missing null guard that turns that hiccup into a hard failure is real though, and it is what is currently blocking this PR. Please leave the YAML schema fixes in this PR as they are.

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body: ## Pull request overview > [!NOTE] > Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review. Adds a regression test and adjusts agent shutdown behavior so `exec` instrumentation does not cause a script’s `EXIT` trap to run prematurely (or more than once), especially when `exec` occurs in a subshell. **Changes:** - Added an automated regression test covering `EXIT` trap behavior with `exec` inside a subshell. - Added a new test fixture script that reproduces the subshell-`exec` scenario. - Updated the agent’s `exec`-instrumentation/shutdown flow and deferred `EXIT` handling to avoid evaluating deferred exit commands from the wrong process. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | tests/auto/test_auto_exec_subshell_trap.sh | New regression test asserting `EXIT` trap fires exactly once and at script end. | | tests/auto/exec_subshell_trap.sh | New fixture script that sets an `EXIT` trap and performs `exec` in a subshell. | | src/usr/share/opentelemetry_shell/agent.sh | Prevents `_otel_end_script` from running during `exec` instrumentation; tracks `EXIT` trap ownership by PID and performs explicit shutdown on `exec` paths. | --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. payload.title: Fix deep docker injection deadlock caused by bash loadable mkfifo ignoring -m 666

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body: ## Pull request overview This PR fixes a deep Docker injection deadlock by preventing use of the bash loadable `mkfifo` builtin in injected containers, where its `-m` handling is subject to `umask` and can create FIFOs too restrictive for cross-UID communication with the out-of-container SDK (issue #3985). **Changes:** - Add `OTEL_SHELL_CONFIG_LOADABLE_BUILTINS` (default `TRUE`) to gate enabling bash loadable builtins in `api.sh`. - Force `OTEL_SHELL_CONFIG_LOADABLE_BUILTINS=FALSE` in deep Docker injection so coreutils `mkfifo -m 666` semantics are used inside containers. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | src/usr/share/opentelemetry_shell/api.sh | Gates enabling loadable builtins behind `OTEL_SHELL_CONFIG_LOADABLE_BUILTINS` to allow opting out of loadable `mkfifo` semantics. | | src/usr/share/opentelemetry_shell/agent.instrumentation.docker.sh | Injects `OTEL_SHELL_CONFIG_LOADABLE_BUILTINS=FALSE` into containers to avoid `umask`-masked FIFO permissions during deep injection. | --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. payload.body:
> @copilot please make sure this is not creating any root span. i think there is a AUTO_INJECTEED or similar env var that shall be set before the . otel.sh, and then unset after. find and it and add it ...

Done. Added `OTEL_SHELL_AUTO_INJECTED=TRUE` before sourcing `otel.sh` in the commit. This follows the same pattern used in `agent.sh` lines 512/514 — when the variable is `TRUE`, no root span is created. `agent.sh` then unsets it after initialization, so the wrapped command's own shell (if it sources `otel.sh`) will behave normally.

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview

This PR aims to reduce fork/exec overhead in the shell instrumentation by opportunistically loading Bash “loadable builtins” (so `rm`/`mkfifo` could run in-process when available) and recommending the corresponding Debian package.

**Changes:**
- Add a Bash-guarded `enable -f` block in `api.sh` to load loadable builtins for `rm` and `mkfifo` (silently no-oping when unavailable).
- Add `bash-builtins` as a Debian `Recommends` dependency.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| src/usr/share/opentelemetry_shell/api.sh | Adds a Bash-only attempt to load loadable builtins for `rm`/`mkfifo` at source time. |
| meta/debian/control | Recommends installing `bash-builtins` to make the loadable builtins available on Debian/Ubuntu. |

payload.title: feat: adopt $/ self-repository syntax for same-repo action references

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview

This PR updates GitHub Actions workflow references within this repository to use GitHub’s new `$/` self-repository syntax instead of `./`, aiming to resolve same-repo actions/workflows against the exact running commit without relying on a checkout for resolution.

**Changes:**
- Updated reusable workflow calls to use `$/.github/workflows/...` in `test.yml`, `publish.yml`, and `ci.yml`.
- Updated same-repo action step references to use `$/actions/instrument/...` in `test_github.yml` and `experiment.yml`.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| .github/workflows/test.yml | Switches CI reusable workflow call from `./` to `$/` self-repo syntax. |
| .github/workflows/test_github.yml | Switches many same-repo action references from `./actions/...` to `$/actions/...`. |
| .github/workflows/publish.yml | Switches CI reusable workflow call from `./` to `$/` self-repo syntax. |
| .github/workflows/experiment.yml | Switches same-repo action reference from `./` to `$/` self-repo syntax. |
| .github/workflows/ci.yml | Switches nested reusable workflow calls from `./` to `$/` self-repo syntax. |
</details>





<details>
<summary>Suppressed comments (4)</summary>

**.github/workflows/test_github.yml:840**
* Same concern as other local action refs in this reusable workflow: `$/actions/instrument/workflow` will be taken from the workflow SHA, not the checked-out `${{ inputs.ref }}`. This job later sources `./actions/instrument/shared/github.sh` from the checked-out ref, so mixing versions can cause subtle incompatibilities when `${{ inputs.ref }}` differs (e.g., `publish.yml` matrix refs).
```
      - uses: $/actions/instrument/workflow
```
**.github/workflows/test_github.yml:935**
* Using `$/actions/instrument/checksuite` decouples the action implementation from the checked-out `${{ inputs.ref }}` in this reusable workflow. If `${{ inputs.ref }}` differs from the workflow commit (e.g., `publish.yml` matrix over multiple commit IDs), the action version and repo contents under test can diverge.
```
      - uses: $/actions/instrument/checksuite
```
**.github/workflows/test_github.yml:956**
* `$/actions/instrument/repository` resolves from the workflow’s commit SHA rather than the checked-out `${{ inputs.ref }}`. Given this workflow explicitly checks out `${{ inputs.ref }}`, keeping `./actions/instrument/repository` avoids action/version skew when `${{ inputs.ref }}` differs (notably in `publish.yml`’s multi-ref matrix).
```
      - uses: $/actions/instrument/repository
```
**.github/workflows/test_github.yml:1160**
* `$/actions/instrument/deploy` will run the action from the workflow commit SHA, even though this job checks out `${{ inputs.ref }}`. If `${{ inputs.ref }}` differs (e.g., `publish.yml` matrix), that can cause deploying/instrumentation behavior to be tested with a different action version than the repo state under test.
```
      - uses: $/actions/instrument/deploy
```
</details>

> @copilot are you sure about this specific file? it tests actions, so it doesnt only have to be this specific repo, but the specific branch and sha as well. is that syntax achieving this?

You're right — `$/` always resolves to the **workflow's own running commit SHA**, not `inputs.ref`. So in `test_github.yml`, which checks out and tests a specific `inputs.ref`, using `$/` would run the action from the wrong commit instead of the one under test.

Reverted `test_github.yml` back to `./actions/instrument/…` in commit `fix: revert test_github.yml to ./ action references`. The other files (`ci.yml`, `test.yml`, `publish.yml`, `experiment.yml`) don't test a specific external ref, so `$/` remains correct there.

| `.github/workflows/autofix.lock.yml` | Regenerated workflow lock file; still missing the described injection of `github.event.workflow_run.id` into the agent prompt context. |
| `.github/aw/actions-lock.json` | Bumps the pinned `github/gh-aw-actions/setup` lock entry to `v0.83.4`. |

**.github/workflows/autofix.lock.yml:301**

```

```

payload.author: copilot-swe-agent
payload.body:
> @copilot i hope there are no manual changes in the lock file? the lock file will be overwritten / recompiled regularly. any manual fixes in there will get lost. which makes me think - why does the tex...

No manual changes in the lock file — it was fully regenerated by `gh aw compile` after editing `autofix.md`. The header confirms this: `# This file was automatically generated by gh-aw (v0.83.4). DO NOT EDIT.`

The text change alone is sufficient because the `actions` toolset was already present in the frontmatter (`toolsets: [context, actions, issues]`). The agent already had the capability to list workflow runs — the problem was purely in the prompt body, which incorrectly told the agent that `triggering-workflow-run-id` was "provided in the context" (it was never injected). The fix removes that false claim and instead instructs the agent to use its already-available `actions` toolset to discover the triggering run ID by querying recent "Analyze" workflow runs. No frontmatter change was needed.

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview

This PR makes `otel_shutdown()` cleanup idempotent by ensuring removal of the remote SDK FIFO does not fail when the FIFO was never created (e.g., when the process exits before `otel_init()` completes). This reduces spurious “instrumentation failure” signals during early termination paths (like failing early in Copilot agent workflows).

**Changes:**
- Update `otel_shutdown()` to use `\rm -f` when removing `$_otel_remote_sdk_pipe`, preventing a non-zero exit when the FIFO is missing.

payload.body:
## Pull request overview

This PR aims to make the GitHub Actions instrumentation “kill switch” activatable via a repository/org-level variable when the internal `__kill_switch` input is not explicitly set, so workflows can be disabled centrally without editing workflow files.

**Changes:**
- Adds a fallback path in `config_validation.sh` that queries the GitHub API for the `OTEL_KILL_SWITCH` Actions variable when `INPUT___KILL_SWITCH` is empty.
- If the variable is found non-empty at repo or org scope, instrumentation exits early with a warning.

payload.body:
> @copilot in the past this produces not the intended result because the vars context will never be resolved in restributable actions for security reasons. please verify against the doc and fix with man...

Good catch. Reverted the `action.yml` defaults back to `''` and instead added GitHub API-based resolution in `config_validation.sh`. When `INPUT___KILL_SWITCH` is empty and a token is available, the script now queries `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/variables/OTEL_KILL_SWITCH` (and falls back to the org-level endpoint) via `curl`. If either returns a non-empty value, the kill switch activates.

Commit: `Resolve OTEL_KILL_SWITCH via GitHub API in config_validation.sh`

## Pull request overview

This PR targets MegaLinter-reported Python issues in the OpenTelemetry shell SDK and deep Python instrumentation layer, aiming to reduce flake8/mypy findings and improve runtime correctness around exception handling and monkey-patching.

**Changes:**
- Add module-level type annotations for `spans` and `observations` in `sdk.py`.
- Replace several bare `except:` clauses with `except Exception:` in `sdk.py`.
- Replace direct assignment to `subprocess.Popen.__init__` with `setattr(...)` in `deep.py` to address mypy’s `method-assign`.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| src/usr/share/opentelemetry_shell/sdk.py | Adds dict annotations and replaces bare `except:` with `except Exception:` (but the described F811 import consolidation for `TraceContextTextMapPropagator` appears incomplete). |
| src/usr/share/opentelemetry_shell/agent.instrumentation.python/deep.py | Uses `setattr` to patch `Popen.__init__` instead of direct assignment to satisfy mypy. |

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview

This PR addresses shellcheck/actionlint findings embedded in hand-written GitHub Actions workflow `run:` blocks (as surfaced by MegaLinter), and adds a narrow actionlint suppression for an intentional empty-string choice in an auto-generated workflow.

**Changes:**
- Rewrites several workflow shell snippets to avoid common shellcheck pitfalls (quoting, `ls | grep`, `xargs` without `-print0`, redirect grouping, etc.).
- Adjusts Docker invocation patterns in workflows to avoid redirect/sudo issues and word-splitting warnings.
- Adds `.github/actionlint.yaml` to suppress a specific syntax-check warning for the generated `agentics-maintenance.yml` only.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 9 out of 9 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| .github/workflows/test_shell.yml | Quotes docker volume/mount args, safer globbing in `mv`, and minor quoting fixes in loops/parsing. |
| .github/workflows/test_package_repositories.yml | Quotes GitHub API URL in `curl` invocation. |
| .github/workflows/test_github.yml | Simplifies alias counting and adjusts quoting/README extraction; **one new quoting regression introduced**. |
| .github/workflows/renovate.yml | Improves quoting/escaping in `gh api` and issue body formatting. |
| .github/workflows/refresh_demos.yml | Replaces `&&/||` chain with `if` and improves jq usage via `--arg`. |
| .github/workflows/publish.yml | Uses `docker load --input` to avoid redirect pitfalls. |
| .github/workflows/build.yml | Replaces `ls | grep` patterns with `find`, hardens `xargs` usage, and refactors redirects; one pipeline remains fragile. |
| .github/workflows/autobackport.yml | Groups multiple `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` writes into a single redirect block. |
| .github/actionlint.yaml | Adds a file-scoped ignore for `string should not be empty` in the generated workflow. |
</details>

payload.author: copilot-swe-agent
payload.body:
> @copilot check this: https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/30251121015/job/89933014152. looks like sdk starting is timing out. find and fix why.

Fixed in the latest commit. The root cause was a missing comma in `sdk.py` line 278 (introduced in `e840b1d`):

```python
# broken
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import ConsoleMetricExporter PeriodicExportingMetricReader
# fixed
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import ConsoleMetricExporter, PeriodicExportingMetricReader
```

This `SyntaxError` prevented the Python SDK process from starting at all. The shell test script then hung indefinitely waiting for a response from a process that had already crashed, until CI killed it after 29 minutes.

payload.author: plengauer
payload.body: @copilot look at https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/30258118277/job/89954740078, this still seems to time out

payload.author: copilot-swe-agent
payload.body:
> @copilot look at https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/30258118277/job/89954740078, this still seems to time out

Fixed in the latest commit. The root cause was that `inject_and_init.sh` line 620 uses `grep -E 'from|import'` to extract import lines from `sdk.py` and prepend them to `sdk_factory.py`. Black formatting had introduced three multiline imports (with parentheses spanning multiple lines) which the grep only partially captured — just the opening line ending in `(` — creating an incomplete, invalid Python import statement at the top of `sdk_factory.py`.

This caused `sdk_factory.py` to fail with a `SyntaxError` on startup. Since it runs with `nohup ... &> /dev/null &`, the failure was silent. The shell then hung indefinitely at `cat /tmp/opentelemetry_shell.github.debug.log` waiting for EOF from a process that had already crashed.

The fix reverts those three multiline imports back to single-line format in `sdk.py`:
```python
# before (Black-wrapped, breaks grep)
from opentelemetry.resource.detector.azure.app_service import (
    AzureAppServiceResourceDetector,
)

# after (single-line, compatible with inject_and_init.sh)
from opentelemetry.resource.detector.azure.app_service import AzureAppServiceResourceDetector
```

payload.author: copilot-swe-agent
payload.body:
> @copilot check out the failing test. it looks like its not resolving correctly. please fix.

Fixed in the latest commit. The root cause is that GitHub doesn't allow `github.*` context in `uses:` fields (validated at template load time, not step execution time).

The solution adds a preceding `run:` step that uses `$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH` (available in composite action `run:` steps) to create a workspace symlink:
```bash
ln -s "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/../deploy-local" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.deploy-local"
```
Then `uses: ./.deploy-local` resolves via that symlink. This correctly points to the action's own sibling directory regardless of whether the action is called locally or from an external repository.

This PR updates the deploy instrumentation action’s workflow-rewrite logic to avoid incorrectly modifying GitHub Actions workflow/job `permissions.actions` when job-level instrumentation is enabled.

**Changes:**
- Refactors the conditional logic that decides whether to set `permissions.actions` to `"read"` for jobs/workflows being modified.
- Attempts to prevent overwriting existing explicit `actions: read|write` permissions at either the job or workflow level.

payload.author: plengauer
payload.body:
@copilot this PR has a failing check that needs fixing:

- **Experiment / `experiment`** — dies at step `Run plengauer/Thoth/actions/instrument/job@aeca67b8`, in `actions/instrument/job/inject_and_init.sh` in the `for node_path in ...` relocation loop (~line 348): `mkdir "$dir_path_new"` is called without `-p`, so it fails with `mkdir: cannot create directory '.../actions/instrument/job/relocated_bin/node20-99f72f0a31e893b02811cbc28d16c42d': File exists`. The script runs under `set -e`, so that exit 1 propagates to `inject_and_init.js`, whose `process.on('close', code => ... reject(code))` has no `.catch()` — the step then crashes with `UnhandledPromiseRejection: ... The promise rejected with the reason "1"` / `code: 'ERR_UNHANDLED_REJECTION'` under Node.js v24.18.0. See https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/actions/runs/32939944050/job/98088681336

  The directory already exists because `instrument/job` runs twice in this job: `.github/workflows/experiment.yml` invokes it explicitly on top of the job-level auto-injection (the same `mkdir` succeeded at `06:52:05` in the first invocation, and by step 4 `type sh` already resolves to `.../actions/instrument/job/bin/sh`). The existing recursion guard (`/tmp/opentelemetry_shell_action_name`) doesn't cover a second explicit invocation. Making the relocation idempotent fixes it — `mkdir -p "$dir_path_new"`, plus ideally an early no-op when that guard file shows the environment is already instrumented.

Two notes so you don't chase the wrong thing:

There is no malformed handle, no `sdk.py` traceback and no `api.sh` problem behind it, so please don't modify the handle-generation code in `api.sh`, `sdk.py` or `agent.injection.http_header.c` to fix this. It is a pre-existing re-entrancy bug that would fail the same way on `main`.
- Everything else on `aeca67b8` is green, the earlier merge conflict is resolved, and the three July review asks all have follow-up commits — including the injected HTTP shim, whose `char *` handle for `SPAN_START` I confirmed is still present at head after the merge. `ci / build / list-python-versions` reports `cancelled` even though all of its steps succeeded; that is being left alone rather than treated as a failure.

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview

This PR fixes a sudo auto-injection edge case where Thoth injected `--preserve-env=...` *after* sudo’s end-of-options separator (`--`), causing sudo to treat the injected option as the command to execute. The change ensures injected sudo options are emitted before the command wrapper, restoring correct behavior for patterns like `sudo -- <command>` used by tools such as `mkcert -install`.

**Changes:**
- Update `_otel_inject_inner_command_args` to treat `--` as an end-of-options marker: consume it and stop parsing wrapper options so injected `more_args` land on the correct side.
- Add an auto test case covering `sudo -- echo hello world` injection behavior.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `src/usr/share/opentelemetry_shell/agent.instrumentation.inner.sh` | Stops option parsing on `--` so injected sudo options (e.g., `--preserve-env=...`) remain sudo options rather than becoming part of the executed command. |
| `tests/auto/test_auto_injection_sudo.sh` | Adds regression coverage for `sudo -- <command>` style invocations. |

payload.author: copilot-swe-agent
payload.body:
> @copilot you did not understand. think harder! i dont want you to seed at all, i want u the find the rootcause of why its missing on busybox / alpine in the first place and fix it!

Addressed in ca40785. Root cause is `_otel_resolve_package_version` using `apk version "$pkg"` parsing that returns no version on Alpine/busybox for installed packages, so `telemetry.sdk.version` became empty. I removed the seeding logic and fixed version resolution to use `apk info -e -v "$pkg"` with proper `name-` and `-rN` stripping, and added unit coverage for this apk path.

payload.author: copilot-swe-agent
payload.body:
> @copilot are u really sure thats the root cause? the retry look should still work, no matter if the artifact is compressed or not. either find the real root cause, really really REALLY confirtm and do...

I double-checked it: the regression is not the compressed vs uncompressed retry lookup.

After `297a251a`, the download path already handled both formats (`gh_artifact_download` unzips when possible and otherwise keeps the raw file), and the workflow reader checked both `traceparent` and `opentelemetry_workflow_run_<attempt>`.

The actual break is the per-job artifact handshake itself. In the old job init loop, two jobs in the same attempt can both miss the workflow artifact, both mint different local traceparents, and both continue with those local values immediately. Even if only one upload ultimately survives (or a later upload wins), the other job has already kept its private root. Workflow-level export and later jobs then read only the surviving artifact, so one workflow attempt gets split across disconnected roots.

That is why I kept the deterministic `run_id + attempt -> traceparent` change instead of reverting it: it removes the inter-job race entirely, while rerun linking still works by deriving the previous attempt’s traceparent from the previous attempt number.

payload.author: anthropic-code-agent
payload.body:
> @claude[agent] you try again, github copilot has failed twice now, this is your time to shine!

Fixed in 888413d. The root cause was a circular deadlock: `_otel_curl_record_api_response_llm_openai` waited for "TERMINATE" from `_otel_pipe_curl_stderr`, but that signal only arrives after the stderr pipe gets EOF, which requires the pipeline (and therefore the response processor itself) to exit first.

The fix:
1. Response processor now breaks after reading "END" instead of looping back for "TERMINATE"
2. `_otel_pipe_curl_stderr` sets `terminated=1` when writing "END" to skip the final "TERMINATE" write (preventing a second deadlock on the forward pipe with no reader)

Also added `test_auto_curl_openai.sh` (requires `OPENAI_TOKEN` env var, calls gpt-4.1-nano) and wired up `secrets.OPENAI_TOKEN` in the smoke test step of `test_shell.yml`.

payload.body: Hello, thanks for contributing for the first time!

payload.author: copilot-swe-agent
payload.body:
> @copilot does this base64 regex include cases like ${{ secrety.my_token || github.token }}? im not sure it includes all special characters that are allowed between ${{ }}

It won’t match `${{ secrety.my_token || github.token }}` (with `secrety`) by design, because we intentionally anchor on `secrets.` only.

It does match `${{ secrets.my_token || github.token }}`. The current decoded regex is:
`\${{[^}]*[[:blank:]]*secrets\.[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+[[:blank:]]*[^}]*}}`
so it allows operators/special chars like `||`, `&&`, `==`, quotes, brackets, commas, etc. around the `secrets.<name>` reference (everything except `}` inside the expression body).

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview

This PR updates the scheduled “Report Failed Workflows” GitHub Actions workflow to ensure the `report` job fails when the reporting pipeline encounters errors (instead of silently continuing), improving reliability of automated issue creation for failing workflows.

**Changes:**
- Enable strict bash error handling (`set -euo pipefail`) so failures in `gh`, `jq`, or the pipeline cause the step/job to fail.
- Replace the base64-encode/decode loop with a `jq -r ... | @tsv` output and a tab-delimited `read` loop to avoid hidden decode/parsing errors.
- Simplify extraction of `workflow_name` and `workflow_url` by reading them directly from the TSV stream.
